chapter: Les Hite, Sebastian's and Duke Ellington
title: Meeting Duke Ellington in 1930 and 1934
summary: Royal first met Ellington in 1930 at the Apex, worked on his films, and filled in with the band repeatedly later.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: It was during the time that you were with Les Hite at Sebastian's Cotton Club that you said you met Duke Ellington?
No, I was with Curtis Moseby, at the Apex.

About 1930, I imagine, was the year. That's when I met Duke Ellington, because I worked with Check and Double Check, picture out there within -- yeah, then after that, he came back out here and did a picture with Mae West called 'My Old Flame,' I believe, and he needed a saxophone player then, so he called me up and I made the picture with them and we made the recording on Victor of 'My Old Flame' with Ivie Anderson. I worked a lot of the surrounding jobs around town here in this area before they went back East. I worked with the Ellington Band then --
Yeah, that's '34. After that, back in

the '40s, I worked with Duke several times after that as replacement for Johnny Hodges. Then I also worked a replacement for Hilton Jefferson on the eastern coast with Duke. And just various times. I was his built-in replacement. Anytime anybody -- anything happened to any of the people that played alto or thereabouts, if I was anywhere within hailing distance, he'd always call me. We had a little mutual admiration society and our own little particular turn-on that we did to each other.
